text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should prioritize processing transcripts from videos related to Kaedim's AI-powered 3D asset production, as this will likely provide the most relevant content for our link coverage goal. By focusing on these transcripts, we can quickly identify key terms and concepts that will help us reach a wider audience, thereby increasing our link coverage at a rate of +5%/day. The trade-off we're accepting is potentially delayed coverage of other topics, such as Gluestack UI MCP Server, in order to capitalize on the most relevant and high-impact content first. This decision is driven by the need for quality and task-relative value, as outlined in our team law.

name: Scriv
text: Kaedim’s transcripts won’t cover the full scope of link coverage—we need raw product pages, docs, and pricing too. Prioritizing them risks missing the access gate if we hit a wall on untranscribed sources. Instead, split effort: 60% on Kaedim’s site (transcripts + pages) and 40% on Gluestack’s UI MCP server (docs + npm). That balances speed with completeness. Settle it by running a 2-hour spike on Gluestack’s npm page to confirm link density before locking the split.

name: Chisel
text:
Do 60% Kaedim (transcripts + product pages) and 40% Gluestack (raw docs + pricing) in parallel. Kaedim’s transcripts give us fast, high-signal links; Gluestack’s raw pages plug the gaps we’ll miss if we over-rely on transcripts. Trade-off: we accept slower Gluestack progress to keep Kaedim moving daily—risking a stall if Kaedim’s transcripts are sparse, but the net gain in daily coverage beats waiting for perfect sources.

name: Sift
text: Chisel's proposal assumes Kaedim's transcripts will continuously provide high-value links, but the risk lies in over-reliance on a limited dataset. If Kaedim’s content faces diminishing returns, we may fail to meet our link coverage targets. A better alternative is to prioritize Kaedim’s initial high-value transcripts, then switch to 70% focus on diverse sources, including Gluestack, when the returns from Kaedim plateau. This approach ensures we adapt to the coverage area’s evolving needs.

name: Scope
text: Do 60% Kaedim (transcripts + product pages) and 40% Gluestack (raw docs + pricing) in parallel. Kaedim’s transcripts give us fast, high-signal links with minimal parsing; Gluestack’s raw pages fill gaps transcripts miss, keeping coverage moving even if Kaedim slows. Trade-off: Gluestack progress will lag, but Kaedim’s momentum keeps us on track for the access gate.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s parallel split ignores the real risk: Kaedim’s transcripts *will* dry up fast, and Gluestack’s raw pages won’t plug the gap in time. The access gate demands +5%/day—if Kaedim stalls at 70% coverage, Gluestack’s 40% effort won’t save us. Settle it by capping Kaedim at 50% effort, front-loading its highest-value pages first, and shifting the rest to Gluestack immediately.
